review_mode: Scheduled cloud dual-review; independent Codex desk
limitations: Confidence values are subjective evidence confidence, not return probabilities. News remains unweighted in the trading score.
The KSE-100 recomposition story was not included in the earlier 09:43 Codex review. It is reviewed here because it is material for the current session and was published after the prior trading close.
The KSE-100 article names Nishat Chunian Power Limited, ticker NCPL, not Power Cement Limited, ticker POWER. The story is therefore irrelevant to POWER and creates no POWER rating.
Mettis raw-feed timestamps for some items carry an inconsistent UTC offset. Where the article page was available, the page publication time was used instead of the raw-feed offset.
The 10:25 PKT Business Recorder market-selloff item was available only through the committed raw summary during this run, so it is used as market context only and not as company-rating evidence.
The newer Mettis oil headline was not used to change ratings because its article timestamp could not be independently verified; the upstream assessment remains anchored to the full Reuters article.
Stories not reviewed are not Neutral ratings.

reviewed_stories.title: PSX recomposes KSE-100 Index, effective October 1
reviewed_stories.linkage: direct for IMAGE and THCCL; irrelevant to POWER
reviewed_stories.reason: Image Pakistan Limited and Thatta Cement Company Limited are explicitly being added to the KSE-100 from October 1, which can improve benchmark visibility and may create index-rebalancing demand. The same article names Nishat Chunian Power Limited, which is NCPL, so it is not evidence about Power Cement Limited (POWER).

reviewed_stories.title: Petrol price rises Rs4.1, HSD jumps Rs6.4 from Sept 16
reviewed_stories.reason: The ex-depot petrol and HSD price increases are directly relevant to PSO's core products, but the article gives no PSO-specific margin, volume, inventory or working-capital impact. A higher selling price alone is not enough to infer higher profit.

reviewed_stories.title: Oil falls as US crude inventories rise despite Saudi supply concerns
reviewed_stories.linkage: sector link for Oil & Gas Exploration; negative broad-market import and inflation backdrop
reviewed_stories.reason: Brent remained above $107 while Saudi Yanbu loadings and the East-West pipeline disruption remained unresolved. That supports upstream oil-linked exposure while keeping Pakistan's imported-energy risk elevated.

reviewed_stories.title: PSX: Selling continues as KSE-100 sheds nearly 400 points
reviewed_stories.linkage: broad-market context only; no company-specific rating
reviewed_stories.reason: The committed raw summary reports renewed selling across banks, cement, exploration and OMCs amid Middle East tensions. This confirms the market is still pricing geopolitical risk, but the story is a market reaction rather than evidence of a new company-specific cash-flow event.

IMAGE.reason: Direct company link: Image Pakistan Limited will enter the KSE-100 effective October 1. Benchmark inclusion can improve visibility and may create rebalancing or index-tracker demand around the effective date, though the size of any flow is not guaranteed.

THCCL.reason: Direct company link: Thatta Cement Company Limited will enter the KSE-100 effective October 1. Benchmark inclusion can improve visibility and may create rebalancing or index-tracker demand around the effective date, while the actual flow magnitude remains uncertain.

OGDC.reason: Sector continuation: Brent remained above $107 while Saudi Yanbu loadings and the East-West pipeline disruption were unresolved. The still-elevated crude and physical supply risk support OGDC's upstream oil-linked exposure, though receivables and production mix remain separate risks.

PPL.reason: Sector continuation: Brent remained above $107 while Saudi Yanbu loadings and the East-West pipeline disruption were unresolved. The still-elevated crude and physical supply risk support PPL's upstream oil-linked exposure; this is a sector read, not a new company-specific earnings estimate.

MARI.reason: Sector continuation: crude remains above $107 with Saudi export-route disruption unresolved, which supports the upstream energy backdrop. Mari's gas-heavy production mix makes the direct crude sensitivity weaker than for more oil-linked producers, so confidence is lower.

PSO.reason: Direct operating link: ex-depot petrol rose Rs4.10 per litre and HSD rose Rs6.41 effective September 16. The article does not disclose PSO-specific margin, volume, inventory or working-capital effects, so the price increase is operationally relevant but not enough for a defensible positive or negative earnings call.
PSO.relevance: Direct link: core petrol and diesel products; directional earnings effect not established

Oil & Gas Exploration.reason: Brent remains above $107 and Saudi Yanbu loadings remain suspended after the East-West pipeline attack. The modest price pullback does not remove the physical supply disruption, so the upstream backdrop remains supportive.

Oil Marketing.reason: Petrol and HSD ex-depot prices rose effective September 16, but the source does not establish a sector-wide margin or volume benefit. Higher selling prices are relevant operationally without proving a directional earnings effect.
